title: 585. Mary, Queen of Scots: The Royal Rivals (Part 2)

sentences.en: In marked contrast to her childhood treatment in Scotland, where she was considered at first a sickly child, unlikely to live, and later a pawn in a dynastic game,
sentences.zh: 与她在苏格兰童年时受到的待遇形成鲜明对比的是，在那里她起初被视为一个体弱多病、难以存活的孩子，后来又成了王朝博弈中的一颗棋子，

sentences.en: even at five years old, Mary was hailed as a figure of romance in France.
sentences.zh: 即便只有五岁，玛丽在法国也受到了浪漫主义色彩的追捧。

sentences.en: A brave little queen who had been forced to flee the barbaric Scots, the cruel English, for the safe arms of all-embracing France.
sentences.zh: 一位勇敢的小女王，被迫逃离野蛮的苏格兰人和残暴的英国人，投入了包容一切的法国那安全的怀抱。

sentences.en: The stage was already set in French minds for the appearance of a childish heroine.
sentences.zh: 法国人的心中早已为这位童年女英雄的登场搭好了舞台。

sentences.en: To their satisfaction, Mary Stuart, with her charm, her prettiness, and the natural docility of youth, was ideal material to be moulded into the playing of this golden role.
sentences.zh: 令他们满意的是，玛丽·斯图亚特凭借她的魅力、美貌以及青春期特有的顺从，成为了塑造这一黄金角色的理想人选。

sentences.en: So that was Lady Antonia Fraser in her celebrated biography of Mary, Queen of Scots.
sentences.zh: 以上内容出自安东尼娅·弗雷泽夫人那本著名的《苏格兰女王玛丽传》。

sentences.en: And she, Tom, is describing the impact that the infant, well not really infant because she's five years old,
sentences.zh: 汤姆，她描述的是这位幼童——其实也不算幼童，因为她已经五岁了——

sentences.en: that the young Scottish queen makes on the French court after she arrives in France in the summer of 1548.
sentences.zh: 这位年轻的苏格兰女王在1548年夏天抵达法国后，对法国宫廷产生的影响。

sentences.en: And in our first episode, you set the scene, didn't you, by talking about the sort of turbulent politics of Mary's childhood,
sentences.zh: 在我们的第一集中，你通过讲述玛丽童年时期那种动荡的政治局势，为我们铺陈了背景，不是吗？

sentences.en: the death of her father and so on when she was only a week old.
sentences.zh: 比如她出生仅一周时父亲就去世了，诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: And then all this complicated political game with Henry VIII and with the French court.
sentences.zh: 还有后来与亨利八世以及法国宫廷之间所有那些复杂的政治博弈。

sentences.en: So just remind us what went on there.
sentences.zh: 所以，请提醒我们当时发生了什么。

sentences.en: Yeah, so the rough wooing.
sentences.zh: 嗯，就是那场“粗暴求婚”。

sentences.en: Henry VIII wanted Mary, Queen of Scots, to marry his son, the future Edward VI.
sentences.zh: 亨利八世想让苏格兰女王玛丽嫁给他的儿子，即未来的爱德华六世。

sentences.en: He thought he'd got the deal.
sentences.zh: 他以为这笔交易谈成了。

sentences.en: Then it got ripped up.
sentences.zh: 结果协议被撕毁了。

sentences.en: He got absolutely irate and sent the English to burn and slaughter and loot, which they then did for eight years.
sentences.zh: 他勃然大怒，派英军去烧杀抢掠，这种暴行持续了八年。

sentences.en: And the impact of this ultimately is that Mary, Queen of Scots, French mother, Mary of Guise,
sentences.zh: 而这一切最终产生的影响是，苏格兰女王玛丽的法国母亲，玛丽·德·吉斯，

sentences.en: who is part of France's leading noble dynasty, she's able to foil the English and secure a French match for her daughter.
sentences.zh: 她出身于法国显赫的贵族王朝，成功挫败了英国人，并为女儿争取到了一门法国亲事。

sentences.en: And when I say a French match, I mean it's the most brilliant French match imaginable.
sentences.zh: 当我提到法国亲事时，我的意思是，这是你能想象到的最辉煌的法国联姻。

sentences.en: Because when Mary Stewart, after a perilous and storm-wracked voyage from Scotland,
sentences.zh: 因为当玛丽·斯图亚特在经历了从苏格兰出发的危险而风暴肆虐的航行后，

sentences.en: and you were very sniffy about her failure to succumb to seasickness, but I think it's historical proof.
sentences.zh: 你对她没有晕船这件事表现得非常不屑，但我认为这是历史事实。

sentences.en: I wouldn't say sniffy, I'd say bracingly sceptical.
sentences.zh: 我不会说是不屑，我会说是持一种令人振奋的怀疑态度。

sentences.en: Go on, continue.
sentences.zh: 继续，请继续。

sentences.en: Young Mary, Queen of Scots, steps onto French soil, and she does so as a future Queen of France.
sentences.zh: 年轻的苏格兰女王玛丽踏上了法国的土地，而她是以未来法国王后的身份踏上这片土地的。

sentences.en: France, because her betrothed is the Dauphin himself.
sentences.zh: 之所以是法国，是因为她的未婚夫正是王太子本人。

sentences.en: And this is the eldest son of Henri II, Henry II, François, or we'll call him Francis, because we're being very Anglophone in our treatment of French names.
sentences.zh: 也就是亨利二世的长子，弗朗索瓦，或者我们叫他弗朗西斯，因为我们在处理法国名字时非常英语化。

sentences.en: I read in your notes, Tom, you've written, I think this is massive punching down from you.
sentences.zh: 我在你的笔记里读到，汤姆，你写道——我觉得你这简直是在欺负弱小。

sentences.en: You've written, he wasn't the hunk he might have been.
sentences.zh: 你写道，他长得并不像他本该有的那样英俊。

sentences.en: And then the next line, one year younger than Mary, so he's four.
sentences.zh: 紧接着下一行写着，他比玛丽小一岁，所以他才四岁。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So I think that's a bit harsh.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这有点刻薄了。

sentences.en: And you mock him as being short.
sentences.zh: 而且你还嘲笑他个子矮。

sentences.en: I mean, all four-year-olds are short, I think it's fair to say.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，所有四岁的孩子个子都矮，我觉得这么说很公平。

sentences.en: Well, he's abnormally short, but Mary is abnormally tall.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他是异常的矮，但玛丽是异常的高。

sentences.en: So there's a disproportion in height.
sentences.zh: 所以身高比例很不协调。

sentences.en: He's got a stutter, and you laugh at him about that.
sentences.zh: 他还有口吃，你还因此嘲笑他。

sentences.en: What do you mean I laugh at him?
sentences.zh: 你什么意思，我嘲笑他？

sentences.en: I'm not laughing at him.
sentences.zh: 我没有嘲笑他。

sentences.en: I'm just setting the historical record straight.
sentences.zh: 我只是在还原历史真相。

sentences.en: And you also mock him, very cruel remarks in the notes about his two left feet.
sentences.zh: 而且你在笔记里还对他那双笨拙的脚发表了非常残忍的评论。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: He can't dance.
sentences.zh: 他不会跳舞。

sentences.en: Mary loves dancing.
sentences.zh: 玛丽热爱跳舞。

sentences.en: He can't dance.
sentences.zh: 他不会跳舞。

sentences.en: Mary's already a brilliant dancer.
sentences.zh: 玛丽已经是位出色的舞者了。

sentences.en: Brilliant dancer.
sentences.zh: 出色的舞者。

sentences.en: She's five, and she's a brilliant dancer, and she can steer the ship single-handedly through a storm.
sentences.zh: 她才五岁，不仅舞跳得好，还能在风暴中独自掌舵。

sentences.en: Unbelievable.
sentences.zh: 简直不可思议。

sentences.en: She's very, very precocious.
sentences.zh: 她非常非常早熟。

sentences.en: But actually, Francis is great.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，弗朗西斯很棒。

sentences.en: He's weedy, but he's plucky.
sentences.zh: 他虽然瘦弱，但很有胆识。

sentences.en: Come on, he's four.
sentences.zh: 拜托，他才四岁。

sentences.en: Actually, the two of them get on tremendously well.
sentences.zh: 其实，他们俩相处得非常好。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: He's not just plucky, but actually very smart.
sentences.zh: 他不仅有胆识，而且非常聪明。

sentences.en: And Mary already has a kind of instinctive sense of what is expected of her, how to play to the gallery.
sentences.zh: 玛丽已经有一种本能，知道别人对她有何期待，以及如何博取众人的欢心。

sentences.en: And so she and Francis, everyone agrees, they make an adorable couple.
sentences.zh: 所以大家都认为，她和弗朗西斯是一对可爱的小情侣。

sentences.en: A charming couple.
sentences.zh: 迷人的一对。

sentences.en: Charming couple.
sentences.zh: 迷人的一对。

sentences.en: Eight's five and four.
sentences.zh: 八岁、五岁和四岁。

sentences.en: No, Tom, don't defend it.
sentences.zh: 不，汤姆，别为这事辩解了。

sentences.en: You love it.
sentences.zh: 你很喜欢这样。

sentences.en: Listen, I'll leave a second.
sentences.zh: 听着，让我说一句。

sentences.en: The king of France, he's like you, he's drunk the iron brew, and he's massively, like, he thinks Mary, Queen of Scots, is brilliant, doesn't he?
sentences.zh: 法国国王，他和你一样，喝了“铁布鲁”汽水，他非常……他觉得苏格兰女王玛丽太棒了，不是吗？

sentences.en: The most perfect child I've ever seen, he says.
sentences.zh: 他说，这是我见过最完美的孩子。

sentences.en: This is a historical testimony, Dominic, which you're sneering at, and which I'm just laying it out as it is.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，这是历史见证，你却在冷嘲热讽，而我只是在陈述事实。

sentences.en: It is what it is.
sentences.zh: 事实就是这样。

sentences.en: And actually, he's so impressed by Mary that he gives orders that she should have precedence over his own daughters in royal processions.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他对玛丽印象深刻，以至于下令在皇家游行中，她应享有高于他自己女儿的优先权。

sentences.en: And this isn't just because she's the betrothed to the Dauphin, but because she's already a queen in her own right.
sentences.zh: 这不仅是因为她是王太子的未婚妻，还因为她本身就是一位女王。

sentences.en: And clearly, you know, she's poised, charming, and regal, all in one.
sentences.zh: 显然，你知道，她沉稳、迷人且高贵，集于一身。

sentences.en: She's a complete package.
sentences.zh: 她简直是个完美的存在。

sentences.en: And also, he says that she should get nicer clothes than his own daughters.
sentences.zh: 而且他还说，她应该穿比他女儿们更好的衣服。

sentences.en: She'd turn up in Scottish fashions.
sentences.zh: 她当时穿着苏格兰风格的服饰出现。

sentences.en: Well, we'll come to the issue of Scottish fashions in due course.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我们稍后会讨论苏格兰服饰的问题。

sentences.en: I mean, I get the sense that you already hate her because of this.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我感觉你已经因为这件事讨厌她了。

sentences.en: No, no, no, I'm objective.
sentences.zh: 不，不，不，我很客观。

sentences.en: And you might think that, you know, the king of France's daughters would hate her, but not a bit of it.
sentences.zh: 你可能以为法国国王的女儿们会讨厌她，但完全不是那样。

sentences.en: Because the French princesses find her so charming, such fun, that they all end up the most tremendous pals.
sentences.zh: 因为法国公主们觉得她太迷人、太有趣了，她们最后都成了最好的朋友。

sentences.en: Oh, lovely.
sentences.zh: 哦，真可爱。

sentences.en: And in fact, I mean, particularly in Lady Antonia's biography, but more generally, the accounts of Mary, Queen of Scots, and her chums, you know, the French princesses, and so on.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我的意思是，特别是在安东尼娅夫人的传记中，更广泛地说，关于苏格兰女王玛丽和她的伙伴们，你知道，那些法国公主们等等的记载。

sentences.en: It's like reading about the kind of the poshest, funnest boarding school yarn.
sentences.zh: 读起来就像是在看那种最时髦、最有趣的寄宿学校故事。

sentences.en: It's a kind of Renaissance Mallory Towers.
sentences.zh: 简直就是文艺复兴版的《马洛里塔》。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And it's great fun, but there's also quite a lot of schooling.
sentences.zh: 这很有趣，但也有不少学业任务。

sentences.en: So Mary, like Elizabeth Tudor, her cousin over in England, is given a very, very good education.
sentences.zh: 所以玛丽和她的表亲英国的伊丽莎白·都铎一样，接受了非常非常好的教育。

sentences.en: I think it's fair to say that unlike Elizabeth, she's not an intellectual.
sentences.zh: 我认为公平地说，与伊丽莎白不同，她不是一个知识分子。

sentences.en: But that's precisely what makes her so charming and fun, because nobody likes an intellectual, do they?
sentences.zh: 但这正是她如此迷人有趣的原因，因为没人喜欢书呆子，对吧？

sentences.en: No, no, no one wants a blue stocking.
sentences.zh: 没错，没人想要一个只会读书的“蓝袜子”。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So she's given an education that would conventionally be regarded as more appropriate to princes than princesses.
sentences.zh: 所以她接受的教育，传统上被认为更适合王子而不是公主。

sentences.en: But that's because she's a queen in her own right, and so therefore she has to be prepared for her role.
sentences.zh: 但那是因为她本身就是一位女王，所以她必须为自己的角色做好准备。

sentences.en: And as John Guy in his brilliant, I think, definitive biography of Mary, Queen of Scots puts it,
sentences.zh: 正如约翰·盖伊在他那本我认为是权威的《苏格兰女王玛丽传》中所写的那样，

sentences.en: what she gets is the equivalent for a prospective ruler of a degree in business administration.
sentences.zh: 她所获得的是相当于未来统治者的工商管理学位。

sentences.en: So she works hard, but she's not a nerd.
sentences.zh: 所以她很努力，但她不是个书呆子。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Her real talent, much more, I think, than for kind of construing Livvy or whatever, although she does that, is for having fun.
sentences.zh: 我认为她真正的天赋，远不止于研读李维之类的著作——尽管她确实读过——而在于享受生活。

sentences.en: So girls just want to have fun.
sentences.zh: 所以女孩们只是想找点乐子。

sentences.en: And Mary, Queen of Scots is the epitome of this.
sentences.zh: 而苏格兰女王玛丽就是这句话的缩影。

sentences.en: And it's such an amazing background for her, because this, of course, is the golden age of the chateau in France.
sentences.zh: 这对她来说是一个非常棒的背景，因为这当然是法国城堡的黄金时代。

sentences.en: Anyone who's been to the Loire and seen the kind of the beautiful chateau there, this is what you're getting.
sentences.zh: 任何去过卢瓦尔河谷并见过那里美丽城堡的人，都会明白这一点。

sentences.en: And Mary and Francis and the royal princesses and all their friends are kind of endlessly processing from Fontainebleau outside Paris to Blois to Chambord on the Loire.
sentences.zh: 玛丽、弗朗西斯、皇家公主们和他们所有的朋友，不断地从巴黎郊外的枫丹白露，辗转到布卢瓦，再到卢瓦尔河畔的香波堡。

sentences.en: She visits them all.
sentences.zh: 她参观了所有这些地方。

sentences.en: And Antonia Fraser can't get enough of it.
sentences.zh: 安东尼娅·弗雷泽对此乐此不疲。

sentences.en: So she exclaims, beautiful gardens, beautiful galleries, so many other beauties.
sentences.zh: 所以她惊叹道：美丽的花园，美丽的画廊，还有那么多其他的美景。

sentences.en: Oh, how charming.
sentences.zh: 哦，多迷人啊。

sentences.en: But her biography is brilliant on this.
sentences.zh: 但她的传记在这方面写得太棒了。

sentences.en: I mean, it brilliantly evokes what she describes it as the kind of the dreamlike quality of Mary's upbringing in France.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它精彩地唤起了她所描述的那种玛丽在法国成长过程中如梦似幻的特质。

sentences.en: She's got ponies, of course.
sentences.zh: 当然，她有小马。

sentences.en: She's got lap dogs.
sentences.zh: 她有哈巴狗。

sentences.en: She's got falcons.
sentences.zh: 她有猎鹰。

sentences.en: She has amazing clothes.
sentences.zh: 她有令人惊叹的衣服。

sentences.en: I mean, the king of France himself has said she has to have the best clothes possible.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，法国国王本人都说过，她必须拥有尽可能最好的衣服。

sentences.en: So she has gloves of dog skin and deer skin.
sentences.zh: 所以她有狗皮和鹿皮手套。

sentences.en: She has velvet shoes of every conceivable color, you know, amazing gowns and dresses and trains.
sentences.zh: 她有各种颜色能想到的天鹅绒鞋子，你知道，还有令人惊叹的长袍、礼服和拖裙。

sentences.en: And she has so many jewels that she needs three brass chests just to hold them.
sentences.zh: 而且她拥有的珠宝多到需要三个黄铜箱子才能装下。

sentences.en: So, as I say, the most tremendous fun.
sentences.zh: 所以，正如我所说，真是太有趣了。

sentences.en: But, of course, you know, in boarding school stories, you're away from home.
sentences.zh: 但当然，你知道，在寄宿学校的故事里，你总是远离家乡。

sentences.en: And so the issue of homesickness is always there.
sentences.zh: 所以思乡的问题总是存在的。

sentences.en: And so people may be wondering, well, Mary's a young girl who's gone to a foreign country.
sentences.zh: 所以人们可能会想，玛丽是一个去到外国的年轻女孩。

sentences.en: Is she ever homesick?
sentences.zh: 她会想家吗？

sentences.en: And I think the answer to that is that to begin with, yes, she misses her mother very badly.
sentences.zh: 我认为答案是，起初是的，她非常想念她的母亲。

sentences.en: And, in fact, Mary of Guise will only once be able to make it out of Scotland and come and see her in France.
sentences.zh: 事实上，玛丽·德·吉斯一生中只有一次能够离开苏格兰去法国看望她。

sentences.en: And the reason for that is that she is literally holding the fort back in Scotland.
sentences.zh: 原因在于她实际上是在苏格兰留守大本营。

sentences.en: You know, she's got Stirling Castle and she's surrounded by people who would quite like to see the back of her.
sentences.zh: 你知道，她守着斯特灵城堡，周围都是些很想让她滚蛋的人。

sentences.en: And the person who'd particularly like to see the back of her is the Earl of Arran, who is next in line to the Scottish throne.
sentences.zh: 而特别想让她滚蛋的人是阿伦伯爵，他是苏格兰王位的下一顺位继承人。

sentences.en: And is this guy who is kind of endlessly shifting and running away from defeats and things like that.
sentences.zh: 这家伙总是摇摆不定，在战败后逃跑之类的。

sentences.en: And so Mary of Guise thinks he's a bit of a loser and she strikes in the spring of 1544.
sentences.zh: 所以玛丽·德·吉斯觉得他是个失败者，她在1544年春天采取了行动。

sentences.en: And the reason that she does then is that by this point, her daughter, Mary, Queen of Scots, is 12 years old.
sentences.zh: 她之所以在那时采取行动，是因为到那时，她的女儿苏格兰女王玛丽已经12岁了。

sentences.en: And this is the kind of age when it's felt that she is able to kind of start picking up the reins of power.
sentences.zh: 这是一个被认为她已经能够开始掌握权力缰绳的年纪。

sentences.en: So Mary of Guise has prepared her tactic well.
sentences.zh: 所以玛丽·德·吉斯很好地准备了她的策略。

sentences.en: She's got people on side and she persuades Arran to resign the regency in exchange for kind of various bungs and benefits and bribes.
sentences.zh: 她争取到了支持者，并说服阿伦辞去摄政王职位，以换取各种好处、利益和贿赂。

sentences.en: But Mary of Guise, this foreign woman, takes his place as the regent of Scotland.
sentences.zh: 但玛丽·德·吉斯，这个外国女人，取代了他的位置，成为了苏格兰的摄政王。

sentences.en: And of course, this is yet another consolidation of French control over Scottish affairs.
sentences.zh: 当然，这又是法国对苏格兰事务控制的进一步巩固。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And even as this is going on back in France, the Queen of Scots is becoming ever more of a French princess.
sentences.zh: 即使在法国发生这一切的同时，苏格兰女王也越来越像一位法国公主了。

sentences.en: Now you say that, Tom, but am I not right in saying that she does dress sometimes in Scottish national dress to amuse the locals?
sentences.zh: 你这么说，汤姆，但我说得不对吗？她有时会穿苏格兰民族服装来逗乐当地人？

sentences.en: So that's nice, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 那挺好的，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And this is defined in France as being basically animal skins, which is not Scottish national dress, but this is what they think.
sentences.zh: 而在法国，这被定义为基本上是兽皮，那根本不是苏格兰民族服装，但他们就是这么认为的。

sentences.en: So it's a kind of it's a kind of mockery.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一种嘲弄。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And she's complicit in it or are they dressing her up against her will or how does it work?
sentences.zh: 她是同谋，还是他们违背她的意愿给她穿上这些？这到底是怎么回事？

sentences.en: A bit of both, I suspect.
sentences.zh: 我猜两者都有。

sentences.en: And I think it reflects the way in which Mary's links to Scotland are starting to fade as she becomes, you know, enters her teenage years.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为这反映了玛丽与苏格兰的联系随着她进入青春期而开始淡化。

sentences.en: So she had travelled to France with a substantial Scottish train.
sentences.zh: 所以她带着一大批苏格兰随从前往法国。

sentences.en: These are all the people who were seasick while she was being poised and regal and not being seasick on the on the journey.
sentences.zh: 这些人就是当她在旅途中保持沉稳高贵、没有晕船时，却晕船的那群人。

sentences.en: But most of her Scottish train has has kind of been sent away.
sentences.zh: 但她的大部分苏格兰随从都已经被遣散了。

sentences.en: So the Scottish attendants who have come with her when Mary's French grandmother, her Guise grandmother, Antoinette de Guise, comes across them.
sentences.zh: 所以当玛丽的法国祖母，她的吉斯家族祖母安托瓦内特·德·吉斯遇到他们时，

sentences.en: She's appalled.
sentences.zh: 她感到震惊。

sentences.en: And she says, we can't have them.
sentences.zh: 她说，我们不能留着它们。

sentences.en: And her exact phrase is they are not as clean as they might be.
sentences.zh: 她的原话是，它们不够干净，可能不太合适。

sentences.en: So essentially she's offended by Scottish standards of hygiene.
sentences.zh: 所以本质上，她是被苏格兰的卫生标准给冒犯了。

sentences.en: Mary has a governess who herself is an illegitimate daughter of James IV, and she's called Lady Fleming.
sentences.zh: 玛丽有一位家庭教师，她本人是詹姆斯四世的私生女，名叫弗莱明夫人。

sentences.en: She's stunningly gorgeous.
sentences.zh: 她美得惊人。

sentences.en: So John Guy describes her as beautiful and voluptuous, and she was known by the French as la belle écossaise, so the beautiful Scotswoman.
sentences.zh: 约翰·盖伊形容她美丽而丰满，法国人称她为“美丽的苏格兰女人”。

sentences.en: And she has a fling with Henry II, the French king.
sentences.zh: 她还和法国国王亨利二世有过一段风流韵事。

sentences.en: And this in itself wouldn't have been particularly a problem, except that she ends up pregnant and thereby precipitates a scandal.
sentences.zh: 这本身倒没什么大问题，但她最后怀孕了，从而引发了一场丑闻。

sentences.en: And so she gets dismissed and sent back to Scotland in disgrace.
sentences.zh: 于是她被解雇，蒙羞回到了苏格兰。

sentences.en: However, it is not a completely Scot-free zone, because Lady Fleming's daughter does remain with Mary in France.
sentences.zh: 不过，这并非完全没有苏格兰人的地方，因为弗莱明夫人的女儿留在了法国，陪伴玛丽。

sentences.en: And she is one of four Scottish girls, all of Mary's age, all of noble birth, all called Mary, who constitute, I guess, I mean, we've now moved on from boarding school stories.
sentences.zh: 她是四个苏格兰女孩之一，都和玛丽同龄，出身贵族，也都叫玛丽，她们构成了——我想，我们现在已经告别寄宿学校的故事了。

sentences.en: These are now Mary's squad.
sentences.zh: 她们现在是玛丽的“小团体”。

sentences.en: This is like kind of gaggle of teenagers in Beverly Hills or whatever.
sentences.zh: 就像比佛利山庄那群十几岁的少女一样。

sentences.en: So you've got the daughter of Lady Fleming, Mary Fleming.
sentences.zh: 所以你有弗莱明夫人的女儿，玛丽·弗莱明。

sentences.en: She's Mary Stewart's cousin.
sentences.zh: 她是玛丽·斯图亚特的表亲。

sentences.en: She is the highest ranking of all the four Marys.
sentences.zh: 她是这四个玛丽中地位最高的。

sentences.en: So you might call her Posh Mary.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以叫她“高贵玛丽”。

sentences.en: Then there's Mary Livingston, who loves hunting, loves dancing, loves archery.
sentences.zh: 然后是玛丽·利文斯顿，她喜欢打猎、跳舞和射箭。

sentences.en: So you might call her Sporty Mary.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以叫她“运动玛丽”。

sentences.en: Then there's Mary Beaton, who is the most beautiful.
sentences.zh: 接着是玛丽·比顿，她是其中最漂亮的。

sentences.en: So you might call her Pretty Mary.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以叫她“漂亮玛丽”。

sentences.en: And then there's Mary Seaton, who knows all about clothes.
sentences.zh: 还有玛丽·西顿，她对服装非常了解。

sentences.en: She's brilliant at hairdressing.
sentences.zh: 她非常擅长梳头。

sentences.en: She can kind of tease any head of hair into an absolute miracle.
sentences.zh: 她能把任何人的头发梳理成奇迹般的发型。

sentences.en: So you might call her Fashion Mary.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以叫她“时尚玛丽”。

sentences.en: And the five of them are completely inseparable.
sentences.zh: 她们五个人完全形影不离。

sentences.en: And they get up to all kinds of scrapes and japes.
sentences.zh: 她们经常一起惹出各种麻烦和恶作剧。

sentences.en: And they're actually a bit like Peter the Great and Marie Antoinette, that they love playing at being common people.
sentences.zh: 她们其实有点像彼得大帝和玛丽·安托瓦内特，喜欢玩平民游戏。

sentences.en: So to quote John Guy, Mary adored making cotignac, a type of French marmalade,
sentences.zh: 引用约翰·盖伊的话，玛丽非常喜欢制作木梨酱，这是一种法式果酱，

sentences.en: putting on an apron and boiling quinces and sugar with powder of violets in a saucepan for hours before laying out the slices of crystallized fruits.
sentences.zh: 戴上围裙，在平底锅里煮上几个小时的木梨、糖和紫罗兰粉，然后铺开那些结晶水果片。

sentences.en: And she gets the four Marys to help her.
sentences.zh: 她还让四个玛丽来帮忙。

sentences.en: And they have a special kitchen that is kind of created in their apartments.
sentences.zh: 她们在自己的公寓里开辟了一个特别的厨房。

sentences.en: And they put on aprons and pretend to be kind of servants or bourgeois women organizing, you know, the housework and the house routines and things like that.
sentences.zh: 她们系上围裙，假装成仆人或中产阶级妇女，打理家务和日常琐事之类的。

sentences.en: It's all such fun.
sentences.zh: 这真是太有趣了。

sentences.en: All very charming.
sentences.zh: 非常迷人。

sentences.en: And it does enable Mary, Queen of Scots, to keep up with her native language because she and the four Marys are all chattering away in Scots,
sentences.zh: 这确实让苏格兰女王玛丽能够保持她的母语，因为她和四个玛丽都在用苏格兰语叽叽喳喳地聊天，

sentences.en: even though all of them by this point speak absolutely fluent French.
sentences.zh: 尽管她们此时都已经能说一口流利的法语了。

sentences.en: And probably it's their, you know, it's their language of choice.
sentences.zh: 而且这很可能是她们的首选语言。

sentences.en: But by the time she's in her mid-teens, I mean, she can probably barely remember any of.
sentences.zh: 但到她十几岁时，我想，她可能几乎记不得什么了。

sentences.en: I mean, she left when she was five.
sentences.zh: 我是说，她五岁就离开了。

sentences.en: She can probably remember nothing of Scotland or virtually nothing.
sentences.zh: 她可能对苏格兰毫无记忆，或者几乎没有记忆。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And presumably that's what the French want.
sentences.zh: 想必这就是法国人想要的。

sentences.en: They wanted to become, you know, she's the wife of the Dauphin.
sentences.zh: 他们想让她成为，你知道，她是王储的妻子。

sentences.en: She's going to become the Queen of France.
sentences.zh: 她即将成为法国王后。

sentences.en: They effectively want her to be French, no?
sentences.zh: 他们实际上是想让她变成法国人，不是吗？

sentences.en: Well, and specifically the Guise family.
sentences.zh: 嗯，特别是吉斯家族。

sentences.en: So her relations on her mother's side, because she is absolutely a key part of the Guise plans, not just for France, but for Europe more generally.
sentences.zh: 也就是她母亲那边的亲戚，因为她是吉斯家族计划中的关键一环，不仅是为了法国，更是为了整个欧洲。

sentences.en: So while Mary's been having this lovely time, you know, with her ponies and making marmalade and so on, her two uncles, we mentioned them before, Francis,
sentences.zh: 所以，当玛丽一直过着这种美好的生活，骑着小马、做果酱等等的时候，她的两个叔叔——我们之前提到过——弗朗西斯，

sentences.en: who's now the Duke of Guise and Charles, who's the Cardinal of Lorraine, they've been busy consolidating their grip on France.
sentences.zh: 现在是吉斯公爵，还有查尔斯，洛林枢机主教，他们一直忙于巩固对法国的控制。

sentences.en: So the Duke, his nickname is Scarface, you know, a battle injury.
sentences.zh: 公爵的绰号是“刀疤脸”，你知道，是因为战斗受伤。

sentences.en: He's very charming, but he's also very hard-nosed, the man of action, veteran of the Italian wars, as we mentioned in the previous episode,
sentences.zh: 他很有魅力，但也非常强硬，是个行动派，意大利战争的老兵，正如我们在上一集提到的，

sentences.en: and a man who in January 1558 shames himself by capturing Calais from the English.
sentences.zh: 而且他在1558年1月从英国人手中夺回加来，让自己名声大噪。

sentences.en: Robbing them of their rightful possession on the French mainland.
sentences.zh: 剥夺了他们在法国本土合法的领地。

sentences.en: So that's very sad.
sentences.zh: 这真是太令人难过了。

sentences.en: And the Cardinal, who is, as we mentioned, the kind of brilliant and fertile schemer, the leading political figure in the French court.
sentences.zh: 而那位枢机主教，正如我们所提到的，是那种聪明而多产的阴谋家，法国宫廷的主要政治人物。

sentences.en: And the pair of them remind me of the Duke and the Cardinal in the Duchess of Malfi, the Jacobean drama.
sentences.zh: 他们俩让我想起了雅各宾派戏剧《马尔菲公爵夫人》中的公爵和枢机主教。

sentences.en: There's a kind of quality, I think, about them that conveys everything that Protestants tend to find sinister about Catholic powers and courts at this time.
sentences.zh: 我认为他们身上有一种特质，传达了新教徒在当时往往认为天主教势力和宫廷所具有的一切阴险之处。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: They have a kind of Borgia vibe to them.
sentences.zh: 他们有一种波吉亚家族的气息。

sentences.en: Yes, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全正确。

sentences.en: And why they want Mary is not just to, you know, if Mary and Francis have children, then their grandchildren will be kings of France, presumably.
sentences.zh: 他们想要玛丽不仅仅是因为，如果玛丽和弗朗西斯有了孩子，那么他们的孙子大概就会成为法国国王。

sentences.en: But their ambitions are higher than that.
sentences.zh: 但他们的野心远不止于此。

sentences.en: They want to forge a kind of Franco-British empire that will be under their thumb.
sentences.zh: 他们想建立一个受他们控制的法英帝国。

sentences.en: And so step by step, they've been putting the building blocks in place.
sentences.zh: 所以他们一步步地打下了基础。

sentences.en: So they have Mary, Queen of Scots, in their grasp.
sentences.zh: 他们已经把苏格兰女王玛丽牢牢掌握在手中。

sentences.en: Her mother, their sister, Mary of Guise, is ruling Scotland as regent.
sentences.zh: 她的母亲，他们的妹妹，吉斯家族的玛丽，正以摄政王的身份统治苏格兰。

sentences.en: And then on the 24th of April, 1558, their niece, Mary, Queen of Scots, marries the Dauphin.
sentences.zh: 然后在1558年4月24日，他们的侄女，苏格兰女王玛丽，嫁给了王储。

sentences.en: And Mary writes to her mother back in Scotland on the morning of her marriage.
sentences.zh: 玛丽在婚礼当天早上写信给远在苏格兰的母亲。

sentences.en: And she says, all I can tell you is that I count myself one of the happiest women in the world.
sentences.zh: 她说，我只能告诉你，我自认为是世界上最幸福的女人之一。

sentences.en: And of course, she's an absolute wow at the wedding.
sentences.zh: 当然，她在婚礼上大放异彩。

sentences.en: Very shockingly, very innovatively, she wears a completely novel colour at her wedding.
sentences.zh: 非常令人震惊且具有创新性的是，她在婚礼上穿了一种全新的颜色。

sentences.en: And that is white in France, unheard of to wear a white dress.
sentences.zh: 那就是白色，在法国，穿白色婚纱是闻所未闻的。

sentences.en: And she does this because she knows that it will suit her complexion and her auburn hair.
sentences.zh: 她这样做是因为她知道这会衬托她的肤色和赤褐色的头发。

sentences.en: Great festivities, gold and silver coins tossed out into the crowds.
sentences.zh: 盛大的庆祝活动，金币和银币被撒向人群。

sentences.en: And the wedding banquet features six giant mechanical ships that kind of glide around the banqueting hall.
sentences.zh: 婚礼宴会上还有六艘巨大的机械船在宴会厅里滑行。

sentences.en: And it's all great fun and absolutely brilliant.
sentences.zh: 这一切都非常有趣，绝对精彩。

sentences.en: And everyone has a wonderful time.
sentences.zh: 每个人都玩得很开心。

sentences.en: Now, what does this wedding mean for Scotland and its continued independence?
sentences.zh: 那么，这场婚礼对苏格兰及其持续的独立意味着什么？

sentences.en: So objectively, publicly, nothing, it would seem.
sentences.zh: 客观地看，公开地看，似乎什么都没有。

sentences.en: So nine days before she gets married, Mary signs and seals a promise to uphold, and I quote, Scotland's freedoms, liberties and privileges.
sentences.zh: 在结婚前九天，玛丽签署并盖章了一份承诺，要维护——引用原文——“苏格兰的自由、权利和特权”。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: But behind the scenes, things are slightly different.
sentences.zh: 但在幕后，情况却略有不同。

sentences.en: So 11 days before she'd signed that pledge that Scottish independence will be maintained,
sentences.zh: 在签署那份维护苏格兰独立的誓言前11天，

sentences.en: Mary had been given another document that had been drawn up by her Guise uncles, which is top secret.
sentences.zh: 玛丽收到了另一份由她吉斯家族叔叔起草的文件，那是绝密的。

sentences.en: Nobody talks about it.
sentences.zh: 没人谈论它。

sentences.en: And it's been drawn up in very florid legal jargon, basically to kind of dazzle Mary, who's still only 15 years old.
sentences.zh: 它用非常华丽的法律术语起草，基本上是为了迷惑当时年仅15岁的玛丽。

sentences.en: But when she puts her seal to it, she is effectively agreeing to a completely bombshell promise that if people in Scotland knew about it would cause outrage.
sentences.zh: 但当她盖上印章时，她实际上同意了一个重磅承诺，如果苏格兰人知道，会引起公愤。

sentences.en: Because what Mary says is that if she dies without an heir, then her husband, Francis, presumably who's going to become the king of France, and all his successors,
sentences.zh: 因为玛丽说，如果她没有继承人就去世了，那么她的丈夫弗朗西斯——大概会成为法国国王——以及他所有的继任者，

sentences.en: so all the future kings of France, will rule as well as the kings of Scotland.
sentences.zh: 也就是未来所有的法国国王，都将同时统治苏格兰。

sentences.en: So Scotland will become part of the French kind of fiefdoMs.
sentences.zh: 所以苏格兰将成为法国领地的一部分。

sentences.en: They also write in that Mary's had this wonderful education, you know, doing her business studies and stuff, all her ponies, all her dog skin gloves and everything.
sentences.zh: 他们还在里面写道，玛丽接受了如此美妙的教育，你知道，学习商业研究之类的，还有她的小马、狗皮手套等等。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And that therefore the Scots owe France a million pieces of gold for it.
sentences.zh: 因此苏格兰人欠法国一百万金币作为回报。

sentences.en: What?
sentences.zh: 什么？

sentences.en: So a very expensive boarding school education.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一次非常昂贵的寄宿学校教育。

sentences.en: That's a very expensive boarding school.
sentences.zh: 那是一所非常昂贵的寄宿学校。

sentences.en: And effectively, it's a blueprint for turning Scotland into a province of France.
sentences.zh: 实际上，这是一份将苏格兰变成法国一个省的蓝图。

sentences.en: Oh, the French.
sentences.zh: 哦，法国人。

sentences.en: God, who would have thought that they would behave like such snakes?
sentences.zh: 天哪，谁会想到他们竟然表现得像毒蛇一样？

sentences.en: And here's the thing.
sentences.zh: 关键在于。

sentences.en: They're not just, that's not even the limit of their ambitions, right?
sentences.zh: 他们不仅仅是，这甚至不是他们野心的极限，对吧？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不。

sentences.en: Because they're also, this is the really shocking thing, they have their eyes on a much greater prize, some would say, which is our own beloved country of England.
sentences.zh: 因为他们还——这是最令人震惊的事情——他们盯着一个更大的奖品，有人会说，那就是我们亲爱的英格兰国家。

sentences.en: Unbelievable.
sentences.zh: 难以置信。

sentences.en: Shocking.
sentences.zh: 令人震惊。

sentences.en: And again, it's Mary who is the key to this plan.
sentences.zh: 而且，玛丽再次成为了这个计划的关键。

sentences.en: Because, and we haven't touched on this yet, but it's a very, very important part of Mary's story.
sentences.zh: 因为——我们还没谈到这一点，但这在玛丽的故事中是非常非常重要的一部分。

sentences.en: We've talked about how she's a steward, the royal line of Scotland, but she also has the blood of the Tudors, the English dynasty in her veins.
sentences.zh: 我们谈过她是斯图亚特家族，苏格兰的王室血统，但她的血管里也流淌着都铎王朝，即英格兰王朝的血液。

sentences.en: And this is because her grandfather, James IV, the guy who had died at the Battle of Flodden, he had married the sister of Henry VIII, Margaret, so Margaret Tudor.
sentences.zh: 这是因为她的祖父詹姆斯四世——那个死于弗洛登战役的人——娶了亨利八世的妹妹玛格丽特，也就是玛格丽特·都铎。

sentences.en: And by 1558, so when Mary is marrying the Dauphin, this has come to take on a potentially enormous dynastic significance.
sentences.zh: 到了1558年，也就是玛丽嫁给王储时，这已经具有了潜在的巨大王朝意义。

sentences.en: So, we left England under the rule of Edward VI, the young Protestant heir of Henry VIII, but he had died in 1553.
sentences.zh: 我们离开英格兰时，它处于亨利八世年轻的新教继承人爱德华六世的统治下，但他已于1553年去世。

sentences.en: And he'd been succeeded by his elder sister, Mary Tudor, who is a Catholic.
sentences.zh: 继位的是他的姐姐，天主教徒玛丽·都铎。

sentences.en: But she, in the months following Mary Stuart's wedding to the Dauphin, has fallen ill and potentially fatally ill.
sentences.zh: 但在玛丽·斯图亚特与王储婚礼后的几个月里，她病倒了，而且可能病得很重。

sentences.en: And so, the question that is being asked in France, as in England, is, well, you know, if Mary Tudor dies, who is going to succeed her?
sentences.zh: 所以，法国和英格兰都在问一个问题：如果玛丽·都铎去世，谁来继位？

sentences.en: Now, of course, she has a younger sister, Elizabeth.
sentences.zh: 当然，她有一个妹妹伊丽莎白。

sentences.en: But the claim of Elizabeth to the English throne is viewed in France, and particularly by the Guise, with contempt.
sentences.zh: 但在法国，尤其是吉斯家族看来，伊丽莎白对英格兰王位的要求是令人蔑视的。

sentences.en: So, as the Cardinal of Lorraine, the subtle, one might almost say sinister, power player at the French court, points out,
sentences.zh: 正如洛林枢机主教——法国宫廷中那位微妙的，甚至可以说是阴险的权力玩家——指出的那样，

sentences.en: Elizabeth is the daughter of a witch, namely Anne Boleyn, who had been put to death by Henry VIII, and her daughter, Elizabeth,
sentences.zh: 伊丽莎白是女巫安妮·博林的女儿，安妮·博林被亨利八世处死，而她的女儿伊丽莎白，

sentences.en: had been declared a bastard by Act of Parliament in 1536.
sentences.zh: 在1536年被议会法案宣布为私生女。

sentences.en: So, she seems to be ruled out of the succession, in the opinion of the Guise.
sentences.zh: 所以，在吉斯家族看来，她似乎被排除在继承权之外了。

sentences.en: And worse than that, of course, she's a Protestant, and no cardinal is going to think that a Protestant should succeed to the throne of England.
sentences.zh: 更糟糕的是，她是个新教徒，没有枢机主教认为新教徒应该继承英格兰王位。

sentences.en: And so, the Cardinal of Lorraine argues that the throne should not pass to Elizabeth, but instead to the next in line, who, of course, just happens to be his own niece,
sentences.zh: 因此，洛林枢机主教主张王位不应传给伊丽莎白，而应传给下一顺位继承人，当然，那恰好就是他的侄女，

sentences.en: Mary Stuart.
sentences.zh: 玛丽·斯图亚特。

sentences.en: So, shocking developments.
sentences.zh: 真是令人震惊的发展。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So, that is potentially, I mean, that would be momentous.
sentences.zh: 所以，这可能——我是说，那将是重大的。

sentences.en: I mean, that would give the Guise family control over not one kingdom, but three kingdoMs.
sentences.zh: 我是说，那将使吉斯家族不仅控制一个王国，而是三个王国。

sentences.en: And so, when Mary, bloody Mary, Mary Tudor dies on the 17th of November, 1558, they're straight in there, aren't they?
sentences.zh: 所以，当“血腥玛丽”玛丽·都铎在1558年11月17日去世时，他们立刻就介入了，不是吗？

sentences.en: They say, our niece, Mary, Queen of Scots, the Queen-in-waiting of France, is now the new Queen of England.
sentences.zh: 他们说，我们的侄女，苏格兰女王玛丽，法国的准王后，现在是新的英格兰女王。

sentences.en: And they really mean this.
sentences.zh: 他们是认真的。

sentences.en: I mean, this isn't just a performative gesture, that this is a serious part of their ambitions, of their kind of geopolitical ambition, right?
sentences.zh: 我是说，这不仅仅是一种表演姿态，这是他们野心的一部分，是他们地缘政治野心的一部分，对吧？

sentences.en: I think they do mean it seriously, but of course, there is a slightly performative element, because they want to treat Mary as though she is the Queen of England.
sentences.zh: 我认为他们是认真的，但当然，确实有一点表演成分，因为他们想把玛丽当作英格兰女王来对待。

sentences.en: And so, the English coat of arms starts featuring alongside those of France and Scotland, you know,
sentences.zh: 于是，英格兰的纹章开始与法国和苏格兰的纹章一起出现，你知道，

sentences.en: in the doorways and the crockery and the plates and things that the dauphin is using in his palace.
sentences.zh: 在王储使用的宫殿门口、陶器和盘子上。

sentences.en: And when ushers clear a way for Mary Stuart, you know, going through the chateau or whatever, they are crying out, make way for the Queen of England,
sentences.zh: 当引座员为玛丽·斯图亚特开路时，你知道，穿过城堡什么的，他们会大喊：“为英格兰女王让路！”

sentences.en: which is obviously very heady stuff for Mary.
sentences.zh: 这对玛丽来说显然是非常令人兴奋的。

sentences.en: I mean, brilliant.
sentences.zh: 我是说，太棒了。

sentences.en: She's Queen of Scots.
sentences.zh: 她是苏格兰女王。

sentences.en: She's now the Queen of England.
sentences.zh: 她现在是英格兰女王。

sentences.en: Soon, she's going to be the Queen of France.
sentences.zh: 很快，她就要成为法国王后了。

sentences.en: And that moment arrived very soon, because on the 10th of July, 1559, the French King, Henry II, dies of a sports injury.
sentences.zh: 那一刻很快就到了，因为在1559年7月10日，法国国王亨利二世死于一场运动伤害。

sentences.en: He's been in a tournament, and the lance goes through a gap in his helmet into his eye, and he dies very soon afterwards.
sentences.zh: 他参加了一场比武，长矛穿过头盔的缝隙刺入了他的眼睛，他很快就去世了。

sentences.en: And two months later, on the 15th of September, 1559, Mary's husband is crowned the King of France.
sentences.zh: 两个月后，即1559年9月15日，玛丽的丈夫加冕为法国国王。

sentences.en: And again, Mary is a massive fashion success.
sentences.zh: 玛丽再次在时尚界大获成功。

sentences.en: She wears white.
sentences.zh: 她穿着白色。

sentences.en: She looks dazzling.
sentences.zh: 她看起来光彩照人。

sentences.en: All the other members of the royal family are in black, so they look very dowdy compared to her.
sentences.zh: 王室的其他成员都穿着黑色，所以和她相比显得非常寒酸。

sentences.en: And, you know, the Queen of Scots, who the French claim is the Queen of England, is now also the Queen of France.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，那位法国人声称是英格兰女王的苏格兰女王，现在也是法国王后了。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: To quote John Guy, wherever the French court came to rest and whichever towns it visited, the heraldic arms of Francis and Mary were blazoned with those of England on the gates.
sentences.zh: 用约翰·盖伊的话说，无论法国宫廷驻扎在何处，无论它访问了哪些城镇，弗朗西斯和玛丽的纹章都会与英格兰的纹章一起被装饰在城门上。

sentences.en: She has done very well for herself.
sentences.zh: 她把自己经营得非常成功。

sentences.en: Queen of Scots, Queen of France, Queen of England, and she's, what, about 16 or something, and she's very glamorous and all this.
sentences.zh: 苏格兰女王、法国女王、英格兰女王，她才大概16岁左右，而且非常迷人，诸如此类。

sentences.en: The only slight flaw I can see in this design is that she's not actually the Queen of England.
sentences.zh: 我能看出的这个计划中唯一的小瑕疵是，她实际上并不是英格兰女王。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So this is a big problem for her, because now the person who is the Queen of England is her cousin, Elizabeth Tudor.
sentences.zh: 所以这对她来说是个大问题，因为现在英格兰女王是她的表亲，伊丽莎白·都铎。

sentences.en: And this is the person who, in all the films and the books and the operas and whatnot, is her arch enemy.
sentences.zh: 而这个人，在所有的电影、书籍、歌剧等等作品中，都是她的死敌。

sentences.en: And you can see why that would be the case, right?
sentences.zh: 你可以看出为什么会这样，对吧？

sentences.en: Because if you're Elizabeth I and you've spent your life, you know, being declared a bastard and being locked up in various houses and all of this,
sentences.zh: 因为如果你是伊丽莎白一世，你一生都在被宣布为私生女，被关在各种房子里，诸如此类，

sentences.en: the arrival of this new contender over the channel in France, who's also very glamorous and whatnot,
sentences.zh: 而海峡对岸的法国又出现了一位新的竞争者，她也非常迷人，诸如此类，

sentences.en: if you're Elizabeth, you presumably absolutely hate the very mention of Mary Queen of Scots's name.
sentences.zh: 如果你是伊丽莎白，你大概会非常痛恨听到苏格兰女王玛丽的名字。

sentences.en: Well, I think that what you do initially is to ensure that powers across Europe do not recognise this potential rival to your throne.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为你最初的做法是确保欧洲各地的势力不承认这位潜在的王位竞争者。

sentences.en: And this is exactly what Elizabeth and her diplomats do.
sentences.zh: 这正是伊丽莎白和她的外交官们所做的。

sentences.en: So they ensure that, for instance, Mary Tudor's husband, who was the King of Spain, Philip II, that he recognises Elizabeth as Queen.
sentences.zh: 所以他们确保，例如，玛丽·都铎的丈夫，也就是西班牙国王腓力二世，承认伊丽莎白为女王。

sentences.en: And even though Philip is Catholic and Elizabeth is Protestant, Philip II does recognise her.
sentences.zh: 尽管腓力是天主教徒，而伊丽莎白是新教徒，但腓力二世确实承认了她。

sentences.en: And the reason for that is that he's desperate to keep England on board in his ongoing struggle with France.
sentences.zh: 原因在于他迫切希望在与法国的持续斗争中让英格兰站在自己这一边。

sentences.en: Yeah, of course.
sentences.zh: 是的，当然。

sentences.en: So power politics trumps kind of religious affiliations.
sentences.zh: 所以权力政治胜过了宗教信仰。

sentences.en: This in turn means that the Pope has to recognise Elizabeth because the Pope is under Philip II's thumb.
sentences.zh: 这反过来意味着教皇也必须承认伊丽莎白，因为教皇受制于腓力二世。

sentences.en: And so he has to do what Philip says.
sentences.zh: 所以他必须听从腓力的指示。

sentences.en: And it's also implicitly agreed, even by the French themselves, because on the 2nd of April, 1559,
sentences.zh: 而且这在某种程度上也得到了法国人自己的默认，因为在1559年4月2日，

sentences.en: they sign a treaty with England, the Treaty of Cateau-Cumbrésie, which effectively is the treaty.
sentences.zh: 他们与英格兰签署了一项条约，即《卡托-康布雷齐条约》，这实际上就是那份条约。

sentences.en: I mean, it's kind of complicated, but in its practical effect is that the English acknowledge that they have lost Calais.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这有点复杂，但其实际效果是英格兰人承认他们已经失去了加来。

sentences.en: And the quo for the quid is that the French implicitly accept that Elizabeth is Queen of England.
sentences.zh: 而作为交换条件，法国人默认接受了伊丽莎白是英格兰女王的事实。

sentences.en: And obviously, this is terrible news for Mary, because not only has her claim to the English throne been sign-lined,
sentences.zh: 显然，这对玛丽来说是个糟糕的消息，因为她对英格兰王位的要求不仅被边缘化了，

sentences.en: but actually the guys who have signed this treaty with the English are her own uncles, the Guise, the people who've been saying, you're the Queen of England.
sentences.zh: 而且实际上，那些与英格兰人签署条约的人正是她自己的叔叔，吉斯家族，那些一直说“你是英格兰女王”的人。

sentences.en: Because it was the Duke of Guise who had captured Calais, and so he wants to confirm his military achievement.
sentences.zh: 因为正是吉斯公爵夺取了加来，所以他想确认自己的军事成就。

sentences.en: And it's doubly bad for Mary, because all the kind of claims to the English throne, as you said, it's alienated Elizabeth,
sentences.zh: 这对玛丽来说是双重打击，因为正如你所说，所有这些对英格兰王位的要求疏远了伊丽莎白，

sentences.en: but it's particularly alienated two key operators at the English court.
sentences.zh: 但它尤其疏远了英格兰宫廷里的两个关键人物。

sentences.en: And one of these is a guy called Sir Nicholas Throckmorton, who is Elizabeth's ambassador to France,
sentences.zh: 其中之一是尼古拉斯·思罗克莫顿爵士，他是伊丽莎白驻法国的大使，

sentences.en: who is a very, very committed, hot Protestant, and therefore very opposed to the idea of England having another Catholic queen.
sentences.zh: 他是一个非常坚定、激进的新教徒，因此非常反对英格兰再拥有一位天主教女王的想法。

sentences.en: And he has been very busy making copies of Mary's offensive heraldic arMs.
sentences.zh: 他一直忙于复印玛丽那些冒犯性的纹章。

sentences.en: So all these ones with England's English coat of arms being courted with the French and Scottish coat of arMs.
sentences.zh: 就是那些将英格兰的纹章与法国和苏格兰的纹章并列的纹章。

sentences.en: And he's sending them back to London.
sentences.zh: 他把这些复印件寄回了伦敦。

sentences.en: And there they are being read by Elizabeth's most trusted servant,
sentences.zh: 在那里，它们被伊丽莎白最信任的仆人阅读，

sentences.en: her chief minister, who is a man called William Cecil, who, like Throckmorton, is a very, very committed Protestant.
sentences.zh: 也就是她的首席大臣威廉·塞西尔，他像思罗克莫顿一样，是一位非常坚定的新教徒。

sentences.en: He's passionately loyal to Elizabeth, but he's even more passionately loyal, I would say, to the Protestant cause.
sentences.zh: 他热情地效忠于伊丽莎白，但我认为，他甚至更热情地效忠于新教事业。

sentences.en: And he's also a man who's long been interested in Scottish affairs, because he had fought with Edward Seymour,
sentences.zh: 他也是一个长期关注苏格兰事务的人，因为他曾与萨默塞特公爵爱德华·西摩一起参加过平基战役，

sentences.en: the Duke of Somerset at the Battle of Pinky, the kind of the disastrous defeat that in a way had precipitated Mary going to France.
sentences.zh: 那场灾难性的失败在某种程度上促成了玛丽前往法国。

sentences.en: So these two Protestants, with the ear of Elizabeth, they loathe Mary and they see her as a potentially mortal threat,
sentences.zh: 所以这两个深受伊丽莎白信任的新教徒，他们憎恨玛丽，并将她视为潜在的致命威胁，

sentences.en: not just to Elizabeth, but to the Protestant cause in England.
sentences.zh: 不仅是对伊丽莎白，也是对英格兰的新教事业。

sentences.en: And so they are completely committed to stopping the Catholic Mary ever succeeding to the English throne.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们完全致力于阻止天主教徒玛丽继承英格兰王位。

sentences.en: And they're so committed to that that actually it's Cecil's real ambition is not just to stop Mary becoming Queen of England, but to topple her from her Scottish throne.
sentences.zh: 他们对此如此执着，以至于塞西尔真正的野心不仅是阻止玛丽成为英格兰女王，还要将她从苏格兰王位上拉下来。

sentences.en: So Mary, I think, is oblivious to this, but she has made herself an enemy who, as events will prove, is as subtle and dangerous an enemy as any queen could have.
sentences.zh: 所以玛丽对此一无所知，但她已经为自己树立了一个敌人，正如事态发展所证明的那样，这是任何女王所能遇到的最狡猾、最危险的敌人。

sentences.en: And while this has been going on, of course, there have been tumultuous events in Scotland, back in her homeland,
sentences.zh: 而在这一切发生的同时，当然，在她的故乡苏格兰也发生了动荡的事件，

sentences.en: events that threaten not just the future of Catholicism in Scotland, but Mary's own survival as queen.
sentences.zh: 这些事件不仅威胁到苏格兰天主教的未来，也威胁到玛丽作为女王的生存。

sentences.zh: 是违背自然的。

sentences.en: Now, that was an archive recording of a Scot, an author of one of the most famous pamphlets ever written by a Scot.
sentences.zh: 刚才那是一段苏格兰人的档案录音，他是苏格兰人写过的最著名的小册子之一的作者。

sentences.en: I mean, history is littered with famous Scottish pamphlets, but this is probably the most famous.
sentences.zh: 我是说，历史上充斥着著名的苏格兰小册子，但这可能是最著名的一本。

sentences.en: And it's the first blast of the trumpet against the monstrous regiment of women.
sentences.zh: 这就是《反对女性怪物统治的第一声号角》。

sentences.en: And disappointingly, monstrous regiment there actually means the kind of unnatural rule of women.
sentences.zh: 令人失望的是，“怪物统治”在这里实际上指的是女性那种不自然的统治。

sentences.en: I'd always thought of it as being, you know, a military squad of women with bayonets marching towards cannon or something.
sentences.zh: 我一直以为那是，你知道，一队拿着刺刀向大炮冲锋的女性军事小队之类的东西。

sentences.en: Now, it's an author you describe in your notes, Tom, as top feminist and funster, John Knox.
sentences.zh: 现在，这是一位你在笔记中描述为顶级女权主义者和搞笑人物的作者，约翰·诺克斯。

sentences.en: So he's the great sort of godfather of the Scottish Reformation.
sentences.zh: 所以他是苏格兰宗教改革的伟大教父。

sentences.en: He absolutely hates Mary, Queen of Scots, doesn't he?
sentences.zh: 他绝对讨厌苏格兰女王玛丽，不是吗？

sentences.zh: 是的，他讨厌。

sentences.en: But here's the thing, his target in 1558, when he wrote that pamphlet, she wasn't really his target there.
sentences.zh: 但问题是，他在1558年写那本小册子时，他的目标并不是她。

sentences.en: His target was somebody else.
sentences.zh: 他的目标是别人。

sentences.en: Mary Tudor in England and Mary of Guise in Scotland, right?
sentences.zh: 英格兰的玛丽·都铎和苏格兰的吉斯家族的玛丽，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah, principally Mary Tudor.
sentences.zh: 是的，主要是玛丽·都铎。

sentences.en: He basically doesn't like Marys.
sentences.zh: 他基本上不喜欢叫玛丽的人。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's not just women, it's Marys.
sentences.zh: 是的，不仅仅是女性，是叫玛丽的人。

sentences.en: He's not in favour of them at all.
sentences.zh: 他一点也不支持她们。

sentences.en: And he sees definitely Mary Tudor, but also by extension Mary of Guise, as kind of exercising a Catholic tyranny over the whole of Great Britain.
sentences.zh: 他认为玛丽·都铎，以及推而广之的吉斯家族的玛丽，是在对整个大不列颠实行天主教暴政。

sentences.en: And so that pamphlet is a kind of pain, cry of despair and frustration that Catholic rule under these women seems impregnable and that the Reformation threatens to be stillborn
sentences.zh: 所以那本小册子是一种痛苦，是绝望和挫败感的呐喊，因为这些女性统治下的天主教统治似乎坚不可摧，而宗教改革似乎胎死腹中，

sentences.en: in the island.
sentences.zh: 在这个岛上。

sentences.en: And yet, Dominic, you as a bluff Protestant will be thrilled to learn that only two years later, everything had been stood on its head.
sentences.zh: 然而，多米尼克，作为一个直率的新教徒，你会很高兴地得知，仅仅两年后，一切都天翻地覆了。

sentences.en: So by 1560, the authority of the Catholic Church in Scotland has been toppled and actually, as it turns out, decisively defeated.
sentences.zh: 到了1560年，苏格兰天主教会的权威已经被推翻，而且事实证明，是被决定性地击败了。

sentences.en: Protestant reformers like Knox himself, perhaps preeminently Knox himself, have emerged triumphant.
sentences.zh: 像诺克斯本人这样的新教改革者，也许最突出的是诺克斯本人，已经取得了胜利。

sentences.en: And the measure of what Scotland has gone through in those two years is that Alec Ryrie, the great
sentences.zh: 衡量苏格兰在这两年里经历了什么的标准是，亚历克·里里，这位伟大的

sentences.en: historian of British Protestantism in his book, The Origins of the Scottish Reformation, he can
sentences.zh: 英国新教历史学家在他的书《苏格兰宗教改革的起源》中，他可以

sentences.en: describe those two years as not just one of the most extraordinary national transformations in European
sentences.zh: 将这两年描述为不仅是欧洲历史上最非凡的国家转型之一，

sentences.en: history, but he goes on to say that it's arguably the first modern revolution.
sentences.zh: 而且他还继续说，这可以说是第一次现代革命。

sentences.en: He disagrees with you because you claim the first modern revolution took place hundreds of years earlier, and yet he's a famous professor, Tom.
sentences.zh: 他不同意你的观点，因为你声称第一次现代革命发生在几百年前，然而他是一位著名的教授，汤姆。

sentences.en: How could you explain that?
sentences.zh: 你怎么解释这一点？

sentences.en: I think what he probably means there is the first revolution of modern Europe, which is a slightly different way of phrasing it.
sentences.zh: 我认为他可能指的是现代欧洲的第一次革命，这是一种稍微不同的表达方式。

sentences.en: Is that what it is?
sentences.zh: 是这样吗？

sentences.en: I think that is what it is.
sentences.zh: 我想就是这样。

sentences.en: So people may be wondering what on earth has happened.
sentences.zh: 所以人们可能想知道到底发生了什么。

sentences.en: What is this great revolution?
sentences.zh: 这场伟大的革命是什么？

sentences.en: And I guess that as good a way as any of answering that question is to look at the career up until
sentences.zh: 我想回答这个问题最好的方法之一就是看看约翰·诺克斯到目前为止的职业生涯，

sentences.en: this point of John Knox, who was probably the most famous of all Mary Stewart's adversaries.
sentences.zh: 他可能是玛丽·斯图亚特所有对手中最著名的一位。

sentences.en: And so he, like so many of the early Protestants, I mean, there's such a feature of the series we did on Martin Luther.
sentences.zh: 所以他，像许多早期的新教徒一样，我是说，这是我们在马丁·路德系列节目中的一个特色。

sentences.en: He had originally himself been a Catholic priest, and probably he was converted to Protestantism by
sentences.zh: 他本人最初是一名天主教神父，他很可能是被帕特里克·汉密尔顿转化为新教徒的，

sentences.en: Patrick Hamilton, who we mentioned in the previous episode, was Scotland's first Protestant martyr.
sentences.zh: 我们在上一集中提到过，他是苏格兰第一位新教殉道者。

sentences.en: He'd been burnt at St. Andrews in 1546.
sentences.zh: 他于1546年在圣安德鲁斯被烧死。

sentences.en: And the man who presided over that execution, who'd brought Hamilton to trial and then convicted
sentences.zh: 而主持那次处决的人，将汉密尔顿送上审判并定罪，

sentences.en: him, and then set him up on a stake in St. Andrews, strapped with bags of gunpowder.
sentences.zh: 然后把他绑在圣安德鲁斯的火刑柱上，身上绑着火药袋的人，

sentences.en: This was Scotland's leading churchman, a guy called David Beaton, who was the Archbishop of
sentences.zh: 这是苏格兰的首席教会人士，一个叫大卫·比顿的人，他是圣安德鲁斯大主教，

sentences.en: St. Andrews, but was also Scotland's last cardinal, as it will prove.
sentences.zh: 但也是苏格兰最后一位红衣主教，事实证明。

sentences.en: And three months later, Beaton gets killed by five assassins who were out to revenge themselves on Beaton for the death of Patrick Hamilton.
sentences.zh: 三个月后，比顿被五名刺客杀死，他们是为了给帕特里克·汉密尔顿的死报仇。

sentences.en: And they murder him in his own stronghold, the castle of St. Andrews, which is right on the coast, pretty impregnable, and they hang his body from the castle walls.
sentences.zh: 他们在他的大本营——圣安德鲁斯城堡谋杀了他，城堡就在海岸边，相当坚固，他们把他的尸体挂在城堡墙上。

sentences.en: It's been stripped naked.
sentences.zh: 尸体被剥光了衣服。

sentences.en: Then they pull it down.
sentences.zh: 然后他们把它拉下来。

sentences.en: One of the Protestants, who've kind of gathered around to exult over his humiliation, then urinates in the mouth of the corpse.
sentences.zh: 其中一名聚集在一起为他的羞辱而欢呼的新教徒，随后在尸体的嘴里撒尿。

sentences.en: They then salt his body, and they throw it into the most notorious dungeon in the whole of Scotland, which is inside the castle of St. Andrews.
sentences.zh: 然后他们腌制了他的尸体，并把它扔进了整个苏格兰最臭名昭著的地牢里，就在圣安德鲁斯城堡内。

sentences.en: And it's a very deep, bottle-shaped hole.
sentences.zh: 那是一个非常深的瓶状洞。

sentences.en: So once you've been put in it, you can only be got out with a kind of rope.
sentences.zh: 所以一旦你被放进去，只能用绳子拉出来。

sentences.en: And it's dug below the level of the sea, right next to the, you know, where you can kind of hear the distant booming of the waves through the rock.
sentences.zh: 它挖在海平面以下，就在旁边，你知道，你可以听到岩石后面远处海浪的轰鸣声。

sentences.en: And this is, you know, a pointed humiliation of the preeminent Catholic churchman in Scotland.
sentences.zh: 这是一种对苏格兰杰出天主教教会人士的尖锐羞辱。

sentences.en: And yet also a fairly standard night out in St. Andrews, I would say.
sentences.zh: 但我也得说，这在圣安德鲁斯算是一个相当标准的夜晚。

sentences.en: Yeah, well, students at St. Andrews can take us up on that.
sentences.zh: 是的，好吧，圣安德鲁斯的学生们可以反驳我们。

sentences.en: So Knox is obviously thrilled by this.
sentences.zh: 所以诺克斯显然对此感到非常兴奋。

sentences.en: He's one of the Protestants who goes to the castle of St. Andrews, which is now kind of stronghold of Protestantism.
sentences.zh: 他是前往圣安德鲁斯城堡的新教徒之一，那里现在是新教的据点。

sentences.en: He serves the garrison there as its chaplain.
sentences.zh: 他担任那里的驻军牧师。

sentences.en: And they're able very easily to hold out against the Scottish authorities up until the point when Henry II sends a massive task force to Scotland to try and throw the English out.
sentences.zh: 他们非常容易地抵御了苏格兰当局，直到亨利二世派遣一支庞大的特遣部队前往苏格兰试图将英国人赶走。

sentences.en: And this task force has enough men that they can go and capture the castle of St. Andrews.
sentences.zh: 这支特遣部队有足够的人手去占领圣安德鲁斯城堡。

sentences.en: And all the garrison are taken prisoner and they are sent to the galleys and Knox is among them.
sentences.zh: 所有的驻军都被俘虏，他们被送往桨帆船，诺克斯也在其中。

sentences.en: So he gets chained up on the bench.
sentences.zh: 所以他被锁在长凳上。

sentences.en: He has to pull the oars and so on.
sentences.zh: 他必须划桨等等。

sentences.en: And he does this for a year and a half.
sentences.zh: 他这样做了整整一年半。

sentences.en: And finally, he is set free as a result of a personal intervention from the English Protestant
sentences.zh: 最后，由于英国新教国王爱德华六世的个人干预，他被释放了，

sentences.en: King Edward VI, who admires John Knox.
sentences.zh: 爱德华六世很欣赏约翰·诺克斯。

sentences.en: So Knox is set free.
sentences.zh: 所以诺克斯被释放了。

sentences.en: Can't go back to Scotland.
sentences.zh: 不能回到苏格兰。

sentences.en: And so he goes to England, he's given a parish in Newcastle, which he chooses because it's pretty close to Scotland.
sentences.zh: 于是他去了英格兰，在纽卡斯尔获得了一个教区，他选择那里是因为它离苏格兰很近。

sentences.en: And so Protestant refugees can kind of mass there.
sentences.zh: 因此，新教难民可以在那里聚集起来。

sentences.en: You know, it becomes a kind of centre of resistance to Mary of Guise and her Catholic regime in
sentences.zh: 你知道，那里成了反抗玛丽·德·吉斯及其天主教政权的一个中心，

sentences.en: Scotland.
sentences.zh: 在苏格兰。

sentences.en: And Knox thinks Edward VI is brilliant.
sentences.zh: 诺克斯认为爱德华六世非常出色。

sentences.en: He thinks England is brilliant.
sentences.zh: 他认为英格兰非常出色。

sentences.en: He sees it as, you know, the new Jerusalem.
sentences.zh: 他将其视为，你知道，新的耶路撒冷。

sentences.en: Brilliant.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: It's absolutely wonderful.
sentences.zh: 这绝对是美妙的。

sentences.en: Hooray.
sentences.zh: 好极了。

sentences.en: And then, of course, Edward VI dies and is succeeded by Mary Tudor, who is Catholic, who will go on to be called by Protestants Bloody Mary because of her burning of Protestants.
sentences.zh: 当然，后来爱德华六世去世了，继位的是玛丽·都铎，她是天主教徒，后来因焚烧新教徒而被新教徒称为“血腥玛丽”。

sentences.en: And so Knox thinks, ah, this isn't a good place for me.
sentences.zh: 所以诺克斯想，啊，这对我来说不是个好地方。

sentences.en: And so he scrams and he ends up in Switzerland, in Geneva, which has become a kind of godly
sentences.zh: 于是他溜之大吉，最终到了瑞士的日内瓦，那里在约翰·加尔文的庇护下，已经成为一种虔诚的

sentences.en: city of reformed religion under the aegis of John Calvin with Luther, one of the two great figures of the Protestant Reformation.
sentences.zh: 改革宗教之城，加尔文与路德并列，是新教改革运动的两位伟大人物之一。

sentences.en: And if Knox had thought that England was brilliant, he thinks that Geneva is even better.
sentences.zh: 如果说诺克斯曾认为英格兰很出色，那他认为日内瓦甚至更好。

sentences.en: So he described it famously as the most perfect school of Christ that ever was in the earth since the days of the apostles.
sentences.zh: 所以他曾著名地将其描述为“自使徒时代以来地球上最完美的基督学校”。

sentences.en: But he does go back to Scotland from time to time, doesn't he?
sentences.zh: 但他确实时不时地回到苏格兰，不是吗？

sentences.en: A couple of times he goes back, yeah.
sentences.zh: 他回去过几次，是的。

sentences.en: Yeah, because there's now a sort of coterie of Scottish lords who are prepared to protect him.
sentences.zh: 是的，因为现在有一群苏格兰贵族准备保护他。

sentences.en: And is that because they are Protestants themselves now?
sentences.zh: 这是因为他们现在自己也是新教徒吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So basically, the Reformation has swept through Scotland, including the aristocratic hierarchy.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，宗教改革已经席卷了苏格兰，包括贵族阶层。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And in fact, the most significant of these is Mary Stuart's own half-brother.
sentences.zh: 事实上，其中最重要的人物是玛丽·斯图亚特同父异母的兄弟。

sentences.en: So one of the many illegitimate sons that her father, James V, had fathered.
sentences.zh: 也就是她父亲詹姆斯五世所生的众多私生子之一。

sentences.en: And he also is James.
sentences.zh: 他也叫詹姆斯。

sentences.en: So James Stuart, Lord James Stuart.
sentences.zh: 所以是詹姆斯·斯图亚特，詹姆斯·斯图亚特勋爵。

sentences.en: He's often cast as a kind of Machiavelli.
sentences.zh: 他常被塑造成一种马基雅维利式的人物。

sentences.en: And he's certainly, he's kind of a very subtle man.
sentences.zh: 他确实是一个非常精明的人。

sentences.en: He's certainly capable of incredible duplicity.
sentences.zh: 他绝对有能力做出令人难以置信的欺诈行为。

sentences.en: But he is also very sober minded and I think very devoutly Protestant.
sentences.zh: 但他也非常冷静，我认为他是一位非常虔诚的新教徒。

sentences.en: So he, all his kind of his political maneuvering is, I think, in the cause of very strongly held Protestant convictions.
sentences.zh: 所以，我认为他所有的政治操弄都是为了坚定持守的新教信仰。

sentences.en: And so Jenny Wormald, the great Scottish historian who's very down on Mary Stuart, she loves her half-brother.
sentences.zh: 因此，对玛丽·斯图亚特评价很低的伟大苏格兰历史学家珍妮·沃马尔德，她很喜欢这位同父异母的兄弟。

sentences.en: She thinks that Lord James Stuart is brilliant, describes him as a true Stuart, tough, able, masterful, masterful, self-interested.
sentences.zh: 她认为詹姆斯·斯图亚特勋爵非常出色，称他为真正的斯图亚特人：强硬、能干、精明、精明、利己。

sentences.en: And I guess by implication, she's implying that Mary Stuart is none of those things.
sentences.zh: 我想言下之意是，她在暗示玛丽·斯图亚特并不具备这些特质。

sentences.en: And he's great pals for Cecil, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 而且他和塞西尔是好朋友，对吧？

sentences.en: With the guy who's going to become Elizabeth I's great spymaster.
sentences.zh: 就是那个后来成为伊丽莎白一世伟大间谍头子的人。

sentences.en: So this is a really important axis in Mary's story.
sentences.zh: 所以这是玛丽故事中一个非常重要的轴心。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And so this guy who, in due course, will become the Earl of Moray, and that's the name by which he's better known.
sentences.zh: 所以这个后来成为莫里伯爵的人，这也是他更广为人知的名字。

sentences.en: He's a key player in the story of Mary, Queen of Scots.
sentences.zh: 他是苏格兰女王玛丽故事中的关键人物。

sentences.en: And so he is able to provide patronage to Protestants in Scotland.
sentences.zh: 因此，他能够为苏格兰的新教徒提供庇护。

sentences.en: But it's also because Mary of Guise, who's the regent, even though she's Catholic, I mean, she's not a natural fanatic.
sentences.zh: 但这也有一个原因，那就是摄政王玛丽·德·吉斯，尽管她是天主教徒，但她并不是一个天生的狂热分子。

sentences.en: She's not a Mary Tudor.
sentences.zh: 她不是玛丽·都铎。

sentences.en: Her priority, I think, is to keep Scotland secure for her daughter, Mary, Queen of Scots, her dynasty, the Guises, her country, France.
sentences.zh: 我认为她的首要任务是为她的女儿苏格兰女王玛丽、她的王朝、吉斯家族以及她的祖国法国确保苏格兰的安全。

sentences.en: And if that means cutting a bit of slack to Protestants, then she's happy to do that.
sentences.zh: 如果这意味着对新教徒稍微宽容一点，那她很乐意这样做。

sentences.en: Her commitment to, you know, preserving Scotland for the true Catholic faith is kind of fourth on the list, I would say.
sentences.zh: 我会说，她致力于为真正的天主教信仰保护苏格兰，在她的清单上只能排在第四位。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: But then, presumably, what changes everything is the death of Mary Tudor in 1558, and the fact that Elizabeth becomes the Queen of England.
sentences.zh: 但后来，大概改变一切的是1558年玛丽·都铎的去世，以及伊丽莎白成为英格兰女王的事实。

sentences.en: Because Mary was not an old woman.
sentences.zh: 因为玛丽当时并不老。

sentences.en: So she could have lived for 10 or 20 years, and this is Mary Tudor, 10 or 20 years more.
sentences.zh: 所以她本可以再活10年或20年，这是指玛丽·都铎，再活10年或20年。

sentences.en: But with her death and the accession of Elizabeth, the whole kaleidoscope takes another turn.
sentences.zh: 但随着她的去世和伊丽莎白的继位，整个万花筒发生了转变。

sentences.en: Well, why does it take such a turn?
sentences.zh: 那么，为什么会发生这样的转变呢？

sentences.en: Is it basically because England now, between Scotland and France, is ideologically different, and therefore there's a new impetus towards Protestantism in Scotland?
sentences.zh: 基本上是因为英格兰现在处于苏格兰和法国之间，在意识形态上有所不同，因此苏格兰出现了向新教发展的新动力吗？

sentences.en: Why does Elizabeth's succession make such a difference to the story?
sentences.zh: 为什么伊丽莎白的继位对这个故事产生了如此大的影响？

sentences.en: Having a Protestant on the English throne, obviously, is a massive destabilising factor, certainly for Mary of Guise.
sentences.zh: 英格兰王位上有一位新教徒，显然是一个巨大的不稳定因素，对玛丽·德·吉斯来说肯定如此。

sentences.en: And the reason that it's a disaster is that it goes with the grain of trends within Scotland.
sentences.zh: 之所以说这是一场灾难，是因为它顺应了苏格兰内部的趋势。

sentences.en: Her rule, although it's been very competent, and although she's a very effective political operator, she is French, and this has become increasingly unpopular with large swathes of
sentences.zh: 她的统治虽然非常称职，虽然她是一位非常有效的政治操盘手，但她是法国人，这在苏格兰公众舆论的广大阶层中，

sentences.en: Scottish public opinion, and particularly with the Scottish nobility.
sentences.zh: 尤其是苏格兰贵族中，变得越来越不受欢迎。

sentences.en: And so by the time that Elizabeth becomes Queen in England, there are nobles in Scotland who
sentences.zh: 所以当伊丽莎白在英格兰成为女王时，苏格兰的一些贵族

sentences.en: are starting to think that France is playing the role in the national demonology that the
sentences.zh: 开始认为法国在民族妖魔化中扮演的角色，正是

sentences.en: English traditionally have played.
sentences.zh: 传统上由英国人扮演的角色。

sentences.en: So there is one resentful lord describes the alliance with France, the old alliance, as an iron hook that hath caught and killed afore now the most part of our ancestors, which is
sentences.zh: 所以有一位心怀不满的领主将与法国的联盟，即老同盟，描述为“一个已经捕获并杀死了我们大部分祖先的铁钩”，这是一种

sentences.en: a kind of massive rewriting of history.
sentences.zh: 大规模改写历史的行为。

sentences.en: And part of the reason for this isn't just dislike for the kind of heavy-handed character of the French garrisons that are providing Mary of Guise with her muscle in Scotland.
sentences.zh: 这其中的部分原因不仅仅是因为不喜欢那些为玛丽·德·吉斯在苏格兰提供武力的法国驻军那种粗暴的性格。

sentences.en: It's also that she is trying to provide Scotland with the kind of centralised rule that she, as a French aristocrat, takes for granted.
sentences.zh: 这也是因为她试图为苏格兰提供那种作为法国贵族她认为理所当然的中央集权统治。

sentences.en: She thinks this is what is required for a successful modern state.
sentences.zh: 她认为这是一个成功的现代国家所必需的。

sentences.en: And again, Scottish nobles feel resentful of this.

sentences.en: I mean, now, you know, what's she going to do?
sentences.zh: 我是说，现在，你知道，她该怎么办呢？

sentences.en: Her uncles, these arch manipulators and Machiavels, they wanted to stay in France because what they want to do is basically to marry her off to Francis's younger brother, Charles,
sentences.zh: 她的叔叔们，这些精于算计的马基雅维利主义者，他们想留在法国，因为他们想做的是基本上把她嫁给弗朗索瓦的弟弟查理，

sentences.en: who is now the new king.
sentences.zh: 也就是现在的新国王。

sentences.en: But Mary is smart enough already to know there is no prospect of this.
sentences.zh: 但玛丽已经足够聪明，知道这根本没戏。

sentences.en: And the chief problem she faces is her mother-in-law, who Dominic is a link to one of the previous series we did, which is the Medici.
sentences.zh: 她面临的主要问题是她的婆婆，多米尼克，这和我们之前做的一个系列有关，就是美第奇家族。

sentences.en: So Mary's mother-in-law, so the wife of Henry II, is Catherine de' Medici.
sentences.zh: 所以玛丽的婆婆，也就是亨利二世的妻子，是凯瑟琳·德·美第奇。

sentences.en: So she's from the Dukes of Florence.
sentences.zh: 她来自佛罗伦萨公爵家族。

sentences.en: And Catherine de' Medici had always disliked Mary as a kind of tool of the guise.
sentences.zh: 凯瑟琳·德·美第奇一直不喜欢玛丽，认为她是吉斯家族的工具。

sentences.en: You know, Catherine de' Medici is a very, very smart operator.
sentences.zh: 你知道，凯瑟琳·德·美第奇是一个非常、非常精明的操盘手。

sentences.en: I mean, a ruthless operator.
sentences.zh: 我是说，一个冷酷无情的操盘手。

sentences.en: And she does not trust Mary.
sentences.zh: 她不信任玛丽。

sentences.en: She wants her cleared from the chessboard.
sentences.zh: 她想把她从棋盘上清除掉。

sentences.en: And she makes this very clear to Mary.
sentences.zh: 她向玛丽明确表达了这一点。

sentences.en: So just one day after Francis's death, she sends a message to Mary saying, hey, give me back all the jewels.
sentences.zh: 就在弗朗索瓦死后仅仅一天，她就给玛丽传话，嘿，把所有珠宝都还给我。

sentences.en: You know, they're not yours anymore.
sentences.zh: 你知道，它们不再属于你了。

sentences.en: They belong to the Queen of France.
sentences.zh: 它们属于法国女王。

sentences.en: You're no longer Queen of France.
sentences.zh: 你已经不再是法国女王了。

sentences.en: Crikey, she's not messing around.
sentences.zh: 天哪，她真是一点都不客气。

sentences.en: Yeah, she's not.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实。

sentences.en: And so Mary knows there's no way that Catherine de' Medici is going to allow her to marry another of her sons.
sentences.zh: 所以玛丽知道，凯瑟琳·德·美第奇绝不可能允许她嫁给自己的另一个儿子。

sentences.en: The other reason why Mary isn't happy to go along with the schemes of her uncles is that, you know,
sentences.zh: 玛丽不愿顺从她叔叔们计划的另一个原因是，你知道，

sentences.en: she views them as having completely stabbed her in the back because they've signed this treaty of Edinburgh.
sentences.zh: 她认为他们完全是在背后捅了她一刀，因为他们签署了这份《爱丁堡条约》。

sentences.en: You know, they've deprived her of her right to the throne of England.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们剥夺了她继承英格兰王位的权利。

sentences.en: And she feels that they had betrayed both her and her mother.
sentences.zh: 她觉得他们背叛了她和她的母亲。

sentences.en: And so because of that, the obvious solution is that she goes back to Scotland because there, at least, she is Queen of Scots.
sentences.zh: 因此，显而易见的解决办法就是她回到苏格兰，因为至少在那里，她是苏格兰女王。

sentences.en: Do you know what?
sentences.zh: 你知道吗？

sentences.en: She should have stayed in France.
sentences.zh: 她本该留在法国的。

sentences.en: She should have knuckled down, just kind of had a little palace of her own, had a quiet life, a lot of dancing, and she'd have lived to a ripe old age.
sentences.zh: 她本该安分守己，拥有自己的小宫殿，过着平静的生活，跳跳舞，这样她就能长命百岁了。

sentences.en: This is a great mistake that she makes.
sentences.zh: 这是她犯下的一个大错。

sentences.en: Do you know who wouldn't agree with you is Jenny Wormald, the great Scottish historian who also, I think, was herself Catholic.
sentences.zh: 你知道谁会不同意你的观点吗？是伟大的苏格兰历史学家珍妮·沃马尔德，我想她本人也是天主教徒。

sentences.en: She feels that Mary should have gone back immediately to Scotland because the sooner she gets back,
sentences.zh: 她认为玛丽应该立即回到苏格兰，因为她回去得越早，

sentences.en: the better the chance there is of reversing the recent successes of Protestantism in Scotland.
sentences.zh: 扭转苏格兰近期新教势力崛起的局面机会就越大。

sentences.en: And the reason for this is that although many of the leading nobility are now Protestant, the vast mass of people in Scotland are still Catholic.
sentences.zh: 原因在于，尽管许多领军贵族现在是新教徒，但苏格兰绝大多数民众仍然是天主教徒。

sentences.en: So very like England under Henry VIII.
sentences.zh: 这和亨利八世统治下的英国非常相似。

sentences.en: Yeah, of course.
sentences.zh: 是的，当然。

sentences.en: And her status as Queen is still unchallenged.
sentences.zh: 而且她作为女王的地位依然稳固，无人挑战。

sentences.en: But as Jenny Wormald puts it, there is no doubt about the strength and prestige of the House of Stuart and the profound unwillingness of the Scots to challenge it.
sentences.zh: 但正如珍妮·沃马尔德所言，斯图亚特王朝的实力和威望毋庸置疑，苏格兰人对挑战这一权威有着根深蒂固的抵触。

sentences.en: So it's what we were talking about in the first episode.
sentences.zh: 所以这正是我们在第一集里讨论的内容。

sentences.en: Mary, by virtue of being a Stuart, she can demand a kind of loyalty that is instinctive to the vast number of Scots of her subjects.
sentences.zh: 玛丽凭借斯图亚特家族的身份，能够唤起绝大多数苏格兰臣民那种本能的忠诚。

sentences.en: And so that being so, Wormald argues, I think, entirely convincingly, that Mary could have played the part of a Mary Tudor in Scotland.
sentences.zh: 因此，沃马尔德认为——我认为非常有说服力——玛丽本可以在苏格兰扮演玛丽·都铎那样的角色。

sentences.en: You know, she could have gone back.
sentences.zh: 你知道，她本可以回去的。

sentences.en: She could have sought to reverse the Reformation.
sentences.zh: 她本可以寻求扭转宗教改革的局面。

sentences.en: And Wormald is very, very down on Mary because of this.
sentences.zh: 正因如此，沃马尔德对玛丽非常、非常失望。

sentences.en: I think having myself had two girls who at one point were 17,
sentences.zh: 我自己有两个女儿，她们也曾有过17岁的年纪，

sentences.en: I think it's quite a big ask to expect a 17-year-old girl who hasn't been to the country that she's being asked to go back to since she was five years old,
sentences.zh: 我觉得要求一个17岁的女孩，在离开那个国家后就再没回去过，现在却要她回去，

sentences.en: to go back and kind of reverse these seismic developments.
sentences.zh: 去扭转这些翻天覆地的变化，这要求实在太高了。

sentences.en: I think it's quite tough to be down on Mary for having ducked the challenge.
sentences.zh: 我觉得因为玛丽回避了挑战而责怪她，实在有点苛刻。

sentences.en: And I am more sympathetic to Mary for essentially prevaricating.
sentences.zh: 我更同情玛丽，因为她本质上是在拖延。

sentences.en: So rather than hurrying back to Scotland, she goes into mourning for Francis.
sentences.zh: 所以她没有急着回苏格兰，而是为弗朗索瓦哀悼。

sentences.en: So that lasts 40 days.
sentences.zh: 哀悼期持续了40天。

sentences.en: She then goes on a kind of massive tour around France saying goodbye to all her, you know, her relatives and her pals and so on.
sentences.zh: 随后她进行了一次大规模的法国巡游，与所有的亲戚、朋友等等一一道别。

sentences.en: And she is also, throughout this, engaging in kind of massive slanging matches with Nicholas Strogmorton, the English ambassador,
sentences.zh: 在此期间，她还与英国大使尼古拉斯·斯罗格莫顿进行了激烈的言语交锋，

sentences.en: who is trying to pressure her to sign the Treaty of Edinburgh, which she refuses point blank to do.
sentences.zh: 对方试图向她施压，要求她签署《爱丁堡条约》，但她断然拒绝。

sentences.en: However, she is preparing to go back to Scotland.
sentences.zh: 不过，她确实在准备回苏格兰。

sentences.en: And the key figure in her plans is her half-brother, Lord James Stuart.
sentences.zh: 她计划中的关键人物是她同母异父的兄弟，詹姆斯·斯图亚特勋爵。

sentences.en: And the reason for that is that I think Mary instinctively, when in trouble, looks to her family, even though her mother had not let her down, but her uncles have done.
sentences.zh: 原因在于，我认为玛丽在遇到麻烦时，本能地会寻求家人的帮助，尽管她的母亲没能帮到她，但她的舅舅们却帮过她。

sentences.en: So there is a problem with Lord James Stuart, which is, of course, that he's a Protestant and not just a Protestant, but he's, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以詹姆斯·斯图亚特勋爵的问题在于，他当然是个新教徒，而且不仅是新教徒，

sentences.en: he's basically been the kind of the leader of the lords of the congregation.
sentences.zh: 他基本上是“领主会议”的领袖。

sentences.en: You know, but as I say, he is family.
sentences.zh: 你知道，但正如我所说，他是家人。

sentences.en: And Mary is obviously hoping that blood is thicker than water.
sentences.zh: 玛丽显然希望血浓于水。

sentences.en: And sure enough, between them, they arrive at a kind of an agreement compact that, when it's announced, appalls both her geese uncles and John Knox.
sentences.zh: 果然，他们之间达成了一种协议，当消息公布时，让她的吉斯家族舅舅们和约翰·诺克斯都感到震惊。

sentences.en: And the reason for that, the reason that the compact appalls the geese is that Mary promises to recognize the Reformed Church, the Protestant Church that, you know,
sentences.zh: 原因在于，这个协议让吉斯家族感到震惊，是因为玛丽承诺承认归正教会，也就是那个新教教会，

sentences.en: John Knox is kind of now the leading light of, as being Scotland's official church.
sentences.zh: 约翰·诺克斯现在是其领军人物，她承认其为苏格兰的官方教会。

sentences.en: In return, she will be allowed to celebrate the Catholic Mass in her own chapel at Holyrood, which is the Royal Palace in Edinburgh.
sentences.zh: 作为回报，她获准在爱丁堡皇家宫殿荷里路德宫的私人礼拜堂举行天主教弥撒。

sentences.en: And I think there's no real question as to who gets the better of that deal.
sentences.zh: 我认为毫无疑问，谁在这笔交易中占了上风。

sentences.en: I mean, clearly, you know, Mary is selling Catholic Scotland down the river, really.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，很明显，玛丽实际上是在出卖天主教苏格兰。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But at least she'll be able to go back as queen, right?
sentences.zh: 但至少她能以女王的身份回去，对吧？

sentences.en: So, you know, it's a big win for her.
sentences.zh: 所以，这对她来说是个巨大的胜利。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And as a Catholic queen.
sentences.zh: 而且是以天主教女王的身份。

sentences.en: And so she leaves Calais on the 14th of August, 1561.
sentences.zh: 于是，她在1561年8月14日离开了加来。

sentences.en: And with her go her four beloved Marys.
sentences.zh: 随她同行的还有她那四位心爱的玛丽。

sentences.en: And they stand on the deck saying adieu, adieu, bidding tearful farewells to France, mourning the fact that they worry they will never see France again, which is entirely accurate.
sentences.zh: 她们站在甲板上说着“再见，再见”，含泪告别法国，哀叹着担心自己再也见不到法国了，而事实确实如此。

sentences.en: Mary will never see France again.
sentences.zh: 玛丽再也没能见到法国。

sentences.en: They're a bit worried because Mary still hasn't signed the Treaty of Edinburgh with Elizabeth.
sentences.zh: 她们有点担心，因为玛丽还没有和伊丽莎白签署《爱丁堡条约》。

sentences.en: And so they're worried that the English may be, you know, looking out for her to try and take her hostage.
sentences.zh: 所以她们担心英国人可能在盯着她，试图把她扣为人质。

sentences.en: And in fact, as they are going up the Northumbrian coast, one of her transport ships, which is carrying her horses,
sentences.zh: 事实上，当她们沿着诺森伯兰海岸航行时，她的一艘运送马匹的运输船，

sentences.en: gets picked up by an English patrol ship on suspicion of piracy and taken into Newcastle.
sentences.zh: 被一艘英国巡逻船以涉嫌海盗罪拦截，并被带到了纽卡斯尔。

sentences.en: So these horses are impounded and it will take three months for them finally to be sent north to Edinburgh.
sentences.zh: 这些马匹被扣押了，花了三个月时间才最终被送往北部的爱丁堡。

sentences.en: Mary herself, she gets to Scotland, to Leith in record time and takes her five days.
sentences.zh: 玛丽本人以创纪录的时间抵达了苏格兰的利斯，全程只用了五天。

sentences.en: No seasickness, of course, because she's so poised.
sentences.zh: 当然没有晕船，因为她太从容了。

sentences.en: And they arrive off Leith and the harbour is thickly veiled by mist so that Mary, in a kind of, it's pregnant with symbolism,
sentences.zh: 当她们抵达利斯外海时，港口被浓雾笼罩，这充满了象征意义，

sentences.en: can't actually make out the contours of her kingdom through this sea miSt.
sentences.zh: 玛丽透过这层海雾，根本看不清她王国的轮廓。

sentences.en: And John Knox, you know, I mean, he's a man ready to see it as an omen.
sentences.zh: 而约翰·诺克斯，你知道，他是一个随时准备将其视为凶兆的人。

sentences.en: And he wrote the very face of heaven at the time of her arrival did manifestly speak what comfort was brought unto this country with her to wit sorrow, dolor, darkness and impiety.
sentences.zh: 他写道：在她抵达之时，苍天变色，分明预示着她给这个国家带来了什么安慰，那就是悲伤、痛苦、黑暗和不虔诚。

sentences.en: But Dominic, was he right?
sentences.zh: 但是多米尼克，他说对了吗？

sentences.en: Well, we love a bit of darkness and impiety on The Rest is History.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们《余下的历史》节目就喜欢一点黑暗和不虔诚。

sentences.en: And I'm happy to say that next time there'll be loads of both as we explore the melodramatic story of Mary, Queen of Scots, on her return to Scotland.
sentences.zh: 我很高兴地告诉大家，下期节目我们将深入探讨玛丽·斯图亚特女王回到苏格兰后那充满戏剧性的故事，届时会有大量此类内容。

sentences.en: Now, if you cannot wait to hear that story, which is one of the most remarkable we've ever done,
sentences.zh: 现在，如果你迫不及待想听那个故事——这是我们做过的最引人入胜的故事之一——

sentences.en: the great news is that you can hear it and the remaining three episodes of this series by joining our very own group of evangelical reformers,
sentences.zh: 好消息是，你可以通过加入我们自己的福音派改革者团体——“领主会议”，即《余下的历史》俱乐部，在therestishistory.com收听该故事以及本系列的其余三集。

sentences.en: the lords of the congregation, the Rest is History Club at therestishistory.com.
sentences.zh: 所以你还在等什么？

sentences.en: So what are you waiting for?
sentences.zh: 带着这个重磅消息，再见。

sentences.en: And on that bombshell, goodbye.
sentences.zh: 再见。

sentences.en: Bye-bye.
sentences.zh: 再见。
